deck_title: Euler-Meusnier directional normal curvature vs naive mean curvature dilution rig

cards.subtitle: Deterministic Leonhard Euler (1760, Recherches sur la courbure des surfaces) & Jean-Baptiste Meusnier (1776) directional normal curvature law (kappa_n(phi) = kappa_1*cos^2(phi) + kappa_2*sin^2(phi), preserving full principal curvature kappa_1 along the bend direction phi = 0 so kappa_1/kappa_model locks at 1.0000x across all 17 curvature-anisotropy stations u in [0.0000, 1.0000] with 0/17 diluted stations) versus naive scalar mean curvature (H = 0.5*(kappa_1 + kappa_2) = kappa_1/(1+u), which averages away directional curvature and underestimates principal cylinder curvature by kappa_1/H = 1 + u up to 1.2500x at u=0.25, 1.5000x at u=0.50, and 2.0000x on a cylinder at u=1.00 across 16/17 stations) and 64-step geodesic osculating circle evaluation.

Flat planar polygons with zero curvature everywhere
